# SwarmOS TUI v1.25.2

This release makes conversation history genuinely searchable and analysable, and
stops the agent reporting its own guardrails as tool failures.

## Highlights

### History search is over 200x faster

A single unreadable conversation file — one `.json` on disk whose conversation
could not be loaded — caused `SyncFiles` to return an error, which made history
search abandon its FTS index and rescan the entire corpus. Every search. Forever,
for anyone with one bad file. Measured on an 8.1 GB corpus of 19,217 files:

| | per search | heap | results for `limit=5` |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 37.7 s | 6,451 MB | 10,814 |
| after | 0.174 s | 27 MB | 5 |

The wrong result count was the symptom that exposed it: the fallback path never
applied the requested limit. A per-item failure inside a bulk sync no longer
propagates to a caller whose only recovery is to abandon the fast path.

Freshness is now decided from filesystem `mtime` and size rather than by parsing
every file to discover when it changed, and the index state for every file is
read in one query instead of one query per file.

### Tool calls and tool results are indexed for the first time

`searchableConversationBody` walked only user and assistant message `Content`.
Tool calls and tool results were never indexed, so nothing any tool did or
returned had ever been searchable, and `ToolResult.Error` was discarded — making
"failed calls only" unexpressible even in principle.

History is now indexed per segment: one row per message, per tool call and per
tool result, carrying tool name, call ID, role, failure state, runtime-injection
state and timestamp. On a real corpus that is 900,902 segments, including 340,499
tool calls and 340,103 tool results that were previously absent entirely.

A conversation larger than 64 MiB was also skipped outright. Oversized
conversations are now decoded as a token stream and segmented without ever being
held in memory, so a 1.58 GB conversation is searchable.

### HistorySearch gained real query power

All of it on the existing tool — no new tool was added.

- `regex` — Go RE2 patterns, for shapes plain terms cannot express.
- `case_sensitive`, and `fields` to target title, preview, or body.
- `snippet` with bounded context and a per-result cap, so a result shows WHY it
  matched instead of a generic preview.
- `exclude_runtime` — omit runtime-injected pseudo-messages, reusing HistoryGet's
  existing predicate rather than forking the marker list. A `user` role is not
  proof a human wrote it.
- `tool_name`, `tool_outcome`, `segment_kind` — search tool traffic directly, and
  isolate failed calls.
- `stats`, `ngram`, `top_terms` — vocabulary and phrase frequency tables over any
  filtered slice of history, reporting occurrences, containing segments and
  containing conversations separately, because "said 1000 times in one
  conversation" and "said once in 1000 conversations" are different findings.

Every new field's zero value means exactly the previous behavior.

### Friction classification uses evidence, not prose

The classifier that decides whether a tool call experienced real friction now
reads the process exit code it was already being given: a non-zero code is
failure evidence, an explicit zero is success. The pointer's three states are
distinguished, so an absent exit code is never read as success.

Its terminal-prose regex and deduplication fingerprint are bounded to 8 KiB,
preserving both head and tail — terminal diagnostics are emitted after the output
they truncate, so a head-only excerpt would drop exactly the signal being looked
for. A successful multi-megabyte log can no longer be classified as a failure
because the word "timeout" appears somewhere in its body.

Absence of evidence is no longer treated as evidence of failure.

## Fixes

- Read no longer refuses text files whose extension resolves to an unusual MIME
  type; file content is authoritative.
- The sleep blocker no longer fires on `timeout` or `sleep` appearing inside a
  heredoc body.
- The hook applicability cache is keyed by tool name, so tool-scoped hooks are no
  longer pruned permanently by the first unrelated tool call of a session.
- Bash commands that feed one command both a pipe and a heredoc are detected; the
  detector can now block as well as advise, via `SWARM_STDIN_CONFLICT_MODE=block`.
  The default remains advisory: a benchmark measured the shape at 2 of 27,449 real
  Bash calls and found no task-success benefit to blocking that would offset the
  raised cost of a false positive.

## Verification

Performance figures are measured by `BenchmarkIndexedHistorySearchRealCorpus`
against a real 8.1 GB corpus, not a fixture. The earlier `history-probe` command
cannot measure this path — it builds its own search backend and lives in a module
that cannot reach the code it appeared to test.

Source release tag: `tui/v1.25.2`
